This is the kickoff, the first of three sessions on the outbreak management functional requirements."},{"id":"M1:T2","text":"Sure, some background first. Outbreak Management, OM, is the PHIN functional area that's meant to support investigating, monitoring, managing, analyzing and reporting on a health event or an act of bioterrorism. The core of any system supporting OM is being able to collect data on cases and exposures, and to create traceable links between all the appropriate entities. Because if you can trace how it's being transmitted and find the source of the health event, the right response staff can contain it a lot more effectively."},{"id":"M1:T3","text":"Great, that helps. So let's dig into the functional requirements themselves. What are the main areas you need covered?"},{"id":"M1:T4","text":"So the first area is analysis, visualization and report generation."},{"id":"M1:T5","text":"Okay."},{"id":"M1:T6","text":"Basically, systems supporting OM should let investigators produce both aggregated"},{"id":"M1:T7","text":"Right."},{"id":"M1:T8","text":"and individual reports on the affected entities and events."},{"id":"M1:T9","text":"So under analysis, visualization and report generation, investigators need to be able to produce both aggregated and individual reports about affected entities and events, is that right?"},{"id":"M1:T10","text":"Yes, exactly."},{"id":"M1:T11","text":"Next one is system integration and data exchange."},{"id":"M1:T12","text":"Mm-hm."},{"id":"M1:T13","text":"OM information has to be exchangeable"},{"id":"M1:T14","text":"Okay."},{"id":"M1:T15","text":"using established standards"},{"id":"M1:T16","text":"Got it."},{"id":"M1:T17","text":"between the systems that are involved in investigating, identifying, confirming and reporting a health event."},{"id":"M1:T18","text":"And then there's system security and availability."},{"id":"M1:T19","text":"Sure."},{"id":"M1:T20","text":"Security of the OM data includes protecting it from corruption"}]}
